newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power down amid warmth, low loads.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power down amid warmth, low loads.

text.p: Western U.S. spot power prices were mostly lower amid mild weather conditions and low demand, market sources said Monday.
"The weather is very mild in California and seasonal up north," where temperatures have fluctuated within a few degrees of normal for the past few days, said one trader.
The Pacific Northwest will continue to see near normal weather conditions this week, with temperatures rising to slightly above normal by the end of the week, said Weather Services Corp.
Southwest temperatures were expected to be slightly below normal today and tomorrow.

Traders said the outage of Northwest Pipeline Corp's natural gas line in Washington over the weekend had no impact on the power market, with the region now largely relying on abundant supplies of low-cost hydropower for electricity needs.
The Northwest River Forecast Center in Portland, Ore., late Friday confirmed preliminary forecasts for spring runoff of 137 percent of normal at The Dalles dam on the Columbia River in Oregon.
Tuesday firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) was quoted at $11.25-12.25 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $13.00-14.00 for Monday.
Off-peak COB was quoted steady at $6.00-7.00.
Firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was at $10.50-11.50, while off-peak was at $5.50-6.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was at $12.50-13.75, while off-peak was quoted at $6.00-8.00.
Next-day firm, peak power at Four Corners was quoted at $12.50-13.50, while off-peak was at $6.00-8.00.
